author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader can browse the clinic's specialties and the veterinarians holding each
summary: A new single-page specialty directory lists every stored specialty with the veterinarians holding it, each veterinarian by full name. Vets with no specialty do not appear; the page is a directory of specialties, not the full roster.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the specialty directory at GET /specialties.html lists every specialty by its stored name on one page with no pagination
A specialty held by one or more veterinarians shows each holding veterinarian by full name, given name before family name (e.g. 'Helen Leary')
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page
A specialty held by no veterinarian still appears, shown with no veterinarians under it
Specialties, and the veterinarians under each, render in a stable, deterministic order
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2 unchanged)
A navigation entry or any link to the page from another page (may follow as separate work)
notes: New REQ minted; distinct from REQ-VET-001, which lists veterinarians grouped with their specialties — this inverts the grouping. Route is GET /specialties.html (contract detail for system-design to pin in Contracts; kept out of PRD prose to match house style, cf. REQ-VET-001). Full name = given name then family name. Every specialty appears including those held by no vet (narrowest reading of 'every specialty the clinic knows'). Open questions recorded in PRD: (1) which specific stable order; (2) whether a visible entry point follows. file_targets/test_names best-effort; a dedicated SpecialtyController/SpecialtyControllerTests may be preferred at design time.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Read-only specialty directory in the existing vet package. Genuinely new ground only in that it introduces two new contracts, both direct applications of catalog patterns: a SpecialtyRepository (Repository pattern, modeled on owner/PetTypeRepository's name-ordered @Query) and a SpecialtyController (Web controller pattern, modeled on VetController + a Thymeleaf view). No new module, no new pattern, no ADR-worthy trade-off. Contracts table and Implements wiring updated in docs/system-design.md. Key data-model fact: the vet->specialty ManyToMany is owned by Vet with no inverse on Specialty, and the seed holds no unheld specialty, so the full specialty set (AC: an unheld specialty still appears) cannot be derived from the vet graph — it must come from SpecialtyRepository.findAll(). The controller reads all specialties (name order) and all vets (cached VetRepository.findAll()), then inverts Vet.getSpecialties() to group vets under each specialty. Both entities stay unchanged.
integration_points: GET /specialties.html routed by SpecialtyController, rendering vets/specialtyList.html — no nav entry and no cross-page link (NG scope; fragments/layout.html menu is NOT edited)

Controller assembles an ordered java.util.LinkedHashMap<Specialty,List<Vet>> into the model: specialties in stored-name order, vets within each keyed by the Specialty entity (not by name string, avoiding merge if two specialties ever share a name), empty list for a specialty held by no vet
Reuses VetRepository.findAll() (already @Cacheable("vets")); no new query on VetRepository and no inverse mapping added to Specialty
Template reuses existing message-bundle keys (specialties, name, vets, none) so no new i18n keys are introduced

patterns.description: name-ordered lookup query precedent: @Query("SELECT s FROM Specialty s ORDER BY s.name") List<Specialty> findSpecialties(); mirror JpaRepository<Specialty,Integer>
Web controller route + Model + view-name pattern to mirror for the single unpaged /specialties.html route
vet/specialty rendering and #{none} usage to mirror; new template omits the pagination block entirely

risks.risk: Adding a new user-facing message key would fail system/I18nPropertiesSyncTest (REQ-LANG-002), which asserts every locale bundle carries the base key set
risks.mitigation: Design reuses only existing keys (specialties, name, vets, none). If a new heading key is unavoidable, it must be added to messages.properties AND all 9 non-en locale bundles in the same change

risks.risk: Grouping keyed by specialty name would silently merge two same-named specialties; schema places no unique constraint on specialties.name
risks.mitigation: Key the ordered map by the Specialty entity, not its name string

risks.risk: Deriving the specialty set from vets would drop specialties held by no vet, violating AC-4
risks.mitigation: Source the complete set from SpecialtyRepository.findAll(); use vets only to populate holders

notes: Redirected file_targets from the PRD's best-effort VetController/VetControllerTests to a dedicated SpecialtyController/SpecialtyControllerTests + vets/specialtyList.html — the PRD notes explicitly licensed this at design time, and the naming rule (controller prefixed by the surface it serves) plus minimal-surface favor a focused controller over a fourth route on VetController. Package placement stays in vet/ (the package owns 'veterinarians and their specialties'); no new package. Settled the two PRD open questions narrowly: (1) ORDERING — specialties in stored-name order (matches SpecialtyRepository query, the specialties_name index, and the PetTypeRepository precedent); veterinarians within a specialty in last-name then first-name order (deterministic, directory-conventional). This is a narrow design settle, not a product mandate — a product owner may revise the intra-specialty sort without design impact. (2) VISIBLE ENTRY POINT — none added; reachable by URL alone per NG scope, layout menu untouched. No ADR: every choice is an application of an in-force catalog pattern with no hard-to-reverse trade-off. Test note: existing VetControllerTests uses @WebMvcTest + @MockitoBean, which sits in tension with testing-principles' no-mocks rule; that tension is pre-existing and out of scope here — implementer should follow the vet-package's established @WebMvcTest slice-test shape for consistency and raise the no-mocks tension separately if it blocks.

findings.description: All four test methods are named `specialtyDirectoryShould*` but the project's BDD naming school (testing-principles.md § Test Naming) requires the `the` prefix: `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}`. The prd-authoring skill defines numbered edge cases as citable items each with a dedicated test; the test-reviewer checks each number has a corresponding test. The content—'The directory has no navigation entry and no page links to it; it is reached only at its own address. A visible entry point is out of scope here and may follow separately.'—is already stated in the narrative prose (line 137) and further discussed in the Open Questions (lines 200-201). No controller test can assert 'no page links to this URL.' Per review-checks.md, edge-case items are never autofix-eligible on the PRD path; this routes to the product-requirements-expert. Fix: remove item 2 from the Edge cases list. Edge case 1 (stable order) is correct and unaffected.

The first sentence of the REQ-SPC-001 narrative is approximately 33 words, exceeding the 30-word writing standard (review-checks.md §4). Sentence: 'The clinic also publishes the specialties it knows, viewed the other way round from the veterinarian directory: each specialty is named as it is stored and shown with the veterinarians who hold it [REQ-SPC-001].' The replacement text exceeds the 200-character autofix bound for the PRD path, so this routes to the product-requirements-expert. Fix: split at the colon into two sentences, each under 30 words.

The SpecialtyController Contracts row Purpose column is a single sentence of approximately 38 words, exceeding the 30-word writing standard (review-checks.md §4). Comparable rows use shorter descriptions or two sentences (e.g., OwnerRepository). The replacement text exceeds the 200-character autofix bound for design-doc paths, so this routes to the system-design-expert (review-checks.md §Autofix on Design-Doc Paths). Fix: restructure into two sentences, each under 30 words, preserving the behavioral content.

The SpecialtyRepository Contracts row Purpose column contains an inline rationale clause: 'which the vet graph alone cannot supply.' This clause explains why the repository is necessary (the vet graph cannot supply unheld specialties), not what the repository does. Per review-checks.md Prohibited Patterns, why-explanations in system-design.md are prohibited; the Contracts table carries behavioral descriptions, not design rationale. The fix is not autofix-eligible on design-doc paths (prohibited-pattern category). Routes to system-design-expert. Fix: remove the clause; the behavioral description 'returning every specialty in stored-name order, including specialties held by no veterinarian' stands on its own.
